craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta as no-fear-talk, suffering conceded (denial and concession in one breath). Sanskrit-first: vārtā (TALK/report — the verse denies the DISCOURSE of fear, not just the feeling); sati (STAND — suffering stands; fear does not). Rows: 9 (denial + concession held unreconciled — ‘no talk…Even while…’ never resolves, resolved WITHIN per C1), 1 (‘stand’ closes — sthā: what stands is named last), 7 (Lord-vocative L1 — pervasion stated TO him). Close: ‘karma-hosts stand’. Rupture: ‘Even while’ (denial turns to concession — the breath holds both). Rejected: ‘yet suffering remains’ — killed: duḥsaha (hard-to-BEAR) kept hard (Bar 6: never smooth); ‘no fear of rebirth’ — killed: saṃsāra-bhaya-vārtā is fear-talk; ‘hosts of karma’ reordering — killed: terror-causing kept fronted (bhayaṅkara modifies first). Read aloud: YOU, lord, per-VADE my OWN-self — SO there IS no TALK … EV-en WHILE hard-to-BEAR SUFF-er-ing … STAND.

lines: You, Lord, pervade my own self — so there is no talk of transmigration-fear.
Even while hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, and terror-causing karma-hosts stand.
l4.sanskrit_cite: svātmani viśvagaye tvayi nāthe tena na saṃsṛtibhītikathāsti satsv api durdharaduḥkhavimohatrāsavidhāyiṣu karmagaṇeṣu

reads_against.argmap: How can fear be denied while suffering is conceded? → Fear-talk denied while suffering conceded: denial and concession in one breath, resolved within the verse.
c1_essence: Fear-talk is denied while suffering is conceded: with You as Lord pervading own self, no talk of transmigration-fear.
Even though hard-to-bear suffering, delusion, terror-causing karmas stand — no-fear and full-suffering together, resolved within it, not deferred.
The non-dual recognition does not deny affliction; it denies fear of it.
